author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Celine Dion is scheduled to perform her first full concert in six years Saturday, opening a sold-out residency in the Paris suburb of Nanterre. The return follows a long interruption caused by stiff-person syndrome, a rare neurological disorder that can produce severe muscle stiffness and spasms.

Dion announced her diagnosis in 2022 and largely withdrew from public performance. She made a major one-song appearance at the 2024 Paris Olympics opening ceremony, singing from the Eiffel Tower, but the new residency represents a return to a complete concert program. The 58-year-old singer is scheduled to perform 26 shows over the next eight months.

Fans have gathered outside Dion's Paris hotel during two weeks of preparations, and the city has promoted the opening with themed decorations at the venue's metro station, a merchandise pop-up and a large public karaoke event. The residency is expected to draw audiences from around the world. Saturday's opening will be the clearest test yet of Dion's ability to resume sustained live performance after years of treatment and rehabilitation.
dek: The sold-out Paris-area residency begins Saturday and marks the singer's first complete concert program in six years.
headline: Celine Dion prepares first full concert in six years
